Salah\'s Hijri date is an Umm al-Qura estimate. If your community follows a different date, shift it here: every Hijri date, the estimated Ramadan range and the Ramadan reminders move with it. The result is still reported as an estimate, because it is one.
Which script and numerals calendar dates are written in.

The Gregorian date comes from the device clock. The Bangla date is converted with the Bangladesh civil rules revised in 2019, and is only offered for the years those rules are verified for. The Hijri date is estimated from the Umm al-Qura table built into Android and is always labelled as an estimate. None of it needs a network connection.
Sehri and Iftar reminders are configured with the other prayer reminders, so they share one scheduler, one set of permissions and one set of channels.
The Ramadan window below is estimated from this device\'s Hijri calculation. Sehri and Iftar times are the same calculated prayer times the Home screen shows.

Scheduled by the same reminder system as the prayers. They are only ever scheduled for the days the calendar places inside Ramadan, and they are cancelled when Ramadan ends or when you switch them off.

Reminders for each prayer, the sound and vibration each one uses, and whether Azan playback is available. Settings are stored on this device and work offline.

An advanced alternative to the area picker: type a position and an IANA time zone directly. Salah validates the input and stores it on this device only. Coordinates are stored as entered — no country check is applied here.
Check the coordinates and the time zone ID (for example 23.8103, 90.4125 and Asia/Dhaka).
Local astronomical calculation (Adhan Kotlin), computed on this device. It needs no internet connection, no account and no permission.
Every time Salah shows is calculated on this device from your coordinates, the date and the settings below. Changing any option recalculates the timetable.

The method sets the twilight angles used for Fajr and Isha. Changing it changes those times, and can shift Dhuhr and Maghrib slightly as well. These are calculation conventions, not a claim to reproduce any authority\'s published timetable.
Affects the Asr time only. Hanafi Asr is always later than standard Asr.
Only matters where Fajr or Isha can fall outside the night. At Bangladesh\'s latitude it does not change the calculated times.
Optional corrections in minutes, added to the calculated time. Use them to match a local timetable you trust; leave them at 0 to show exactly what the engine calculates.
Saved. Prayer times have been recalculated.

Salah is an offline-first Islamic companion. Gregorian dates come from the device clock, prayer times are calculated locally by an astronomical engine, and prayer reminders are scheduled and delivered without a network connection. The Bangladesh Bangla calendar is converted with the 2019 Bangla Academy rules and the Hijri calendar is an Umm al-Qura estimate, labelled as an estimate wherever it appears. Prohibited-time rules are not configured and Azan audio is not bundled \u2014 each of those is stated in the app where it applies.
This destination exists as a navigation boundary. Nothing is implemented here yet, so no value in this section is presented as a working feature.
Daily times are calculated by the local engine on the Home screen, and prayer reminders are scheduled on this device. Monthly timetables are planned.
Salah schedules reminders from the prayer times it calculates on this device. Everything here works offline and is stored on the device only.

These are two separate permissions and Salah asks for each one only when you press the button. Notification permission lets a reminder appear in the shade. Exact alarms lets a reminder run at the prayer time even while the phone is dozing; without it Salah still schedules the reminder, but Android may run it up to ten minutes late.

Exact alarms are not allowed, so reminders are scheduled with a window instead. They will still arrive, but Android may delay them by a few minutes and a phone in deep power saving may delay them further.
Salah keeps reminders for today and tomorrow up to date, and rebuilds them after a restart.
No reminder is scheduled and Salah has cancelled the ones it had scheduled. Turning this back on schedules the prayers you have enabled below.
Scheduled reminders: %1$d, covering the next %2$d days (today and tomorrow).
No timetable could be calculated for %1$d of those days, so the reminders already stored for them were left untouched rather than dropped.
No reconciliation has run in this session yet.
Salah recalculates the schedule whenever you change a setting here, change your location or calculation method, change the device time or time zone, or restart the phone.
Notifications need a location, because prayer times are calculated from it. Add one under Settings, then open this screen again.
Each prayer can be configured on its own. A reminder can stay enabled while its sound is silent.
No reminder is scheduled for this prayer.
Where the device and its settings allow it.
An additional reminder ahead of the prayer. Off means only the prayer-time reminder is scheduled.
Sunrise is a solar event, not one of the five obligatory prayers, so it is configured separately and is off by default. Its reminder says sunrise, never prayer.

Salah can play a full Azan recording, but no recording is bundled: redistributing one needs rights this project does not have, and a generated tone would not be an Azan. Rather than offer a control that cannot work, Salah plays the notification sound you chose above. Adding a licensed recording is a one-line change to the audio source, and the playback code and its tests already exist.
A licensed recording is bundled, so an at-time prayer reminder also starts playback. Notifications and playback are separate: turning off one never turns off the other.

Do Not Disturb, battery optimisation and the device maker\'s power management all sit between Salah and the screen. Salah schedules reminders with Android\'s supported alarm and notification APIs and does not try to bypass any of them, so a reminder can be delayed or silenced by settings Salah cannot override.

Sounds and vibration live in Android notification channels. Changing a prayer\'s sound here routes it to the matching channel; if you have already customised that channel in system settings, Android keeps your choice.
Reminders are calculated, scheduled and delivered without an internet connection. No account is required and nothing is sent anywhere.

Sehri and Iftar reminders, scheduled from the same calculated times as everything else and only during Ramadan.

Both derive from the calculated Fajr and Maghrib times, so they follow your calculation method and manual adjustments automatically. Salah applies no extra buffer to either, and does not claim to reproduce any authority\'s timetable.

The Qibla bearing is calculated on this device from the stored coordinates. It needs no network and no account.
Set a location to see the Qibla direction.

You are at the point furthest from the Kaaba on Earth, where every direction towards it is the same distance and no single bearing exists.
This device has no magnetometer-backed sensor, so Salah cannot show which way the device is pointing. The bearing above is still exact — use it with a separate compass or the sun.
Hold the device flat. At this angle the compass heading is not reliable, so the dial and the turn are withheld.
Magnetic declination could not be estimated for this location, so the heading is shown from magnetic north and no alignment is claimed.

Android reports that this device\'s magnetic readings are not well calibrated. Moving the device in a figure-eight a few times usually helps. Keep it clear of magnets, speakers and metal, which disturb the reading.

This is a saved position, not a current reading.

This location is the published reference point of the administrative area you selected, not an exact position. The bearing is calculated from that point, and the difference it makes to a Qibla bearing is far smaller than a compass can show.
Approximate location is in use. It is enough for the Qibla: a position error of a few kilometres moves the bearing by only a few hundredths of a degree.
Stored on this device only. Works with no network and no location permission.
IANA zone, for example Asia/Dhaka. Change it if these coordinates are in another zone.

The bearing is exact spherical trigonometry over the stored coordinates. What the dial shows depends on the device: magnetometer quality, nearby magnets and metal, how flat the device is held, and the accuracy of the magnetic-declination model. Salah corrects the heading to true north exactly once and never presents an uncorrected heading as aligned. Treat the dial as good to a few degrees outdoors, and less near large metal objects.
Salah calculates prayer times, the Qibla direction, the Ramadan calendar and the Sehri and Iftar reminders from your coordinates, and everything is computed on this device.
This version of Salah supports locations in Bangladesh only. The bundled area dataset, the calculation settings and the Hijri and Bangla calendars are all Bangladesh-specific.

Prayer times depend on where you are to within a minute, so Salah cannot calculate anything location-dependent until it knows the place and its time zone. Nothing is uploaded: the coordinates stay on this device.
Both options work without a network connection. A device fix needs location permission; choosing an area by hand needs none.

A selected area stores the published reference coordinates of that area — its administrative centre — not your exact position. Prayer times are calculated for that point, so they may differ by a minute or two from your own house.

The location dataset could not be read

Salah reads its list of Bangladeshi divisions, districts and upazilas from files bundled inside the app, and those files could not be read in this build. Without them a location cannot be chosen and prayer times cannot be calculated. This is a build problem rather than a setting: reinstalling a complete build should fix it.
